name: Executive Report
description: A restrained navy-and-gold monthly or quarterly report: serif headings, generous whitespace, KPI cards and print-friendly tables.
note: Initial version: light + dark, four components, print-safe palette.

gold.$description: Secondary accent: rules and KPI deltas.

bundle.guidance:
# Executive Report

A monthly or quarterly report that a busy executive reads in eight minutes and
then forwards. It must survive being printed in black and white.

## Principles

1. **Conclusion first.** Every section opens with the finding in one sentence,
   then the evidence. Never make the reader assemble the point themselves.
2. **Whitespace is authority.** Crowding reads as anxious; the page should feel
   unhurried even when the news is bad.
3. **One number per idea.** A KPI card carries a single headline figure and a
   single delta. If two numbers matter, use two cards.

## Layout grid

Single column, `max-width: 42rem`, `--space-xl` between top-level sections.
KPI cards sit in a flex row of two to four; below `40rem` they stack. Tables
and charts may span to `52rem`. Leave the top of the document to a title
block: report name, period, author, date — nothing else.

## Typography

Headings use the serif family at `--size-h1` / `--size-h2` / `--size-h3`, body
is Inter at `--size-body` with `--line-body`. The generous body size is
deliberate; do not shrink it to fit more in. Numbers in KPI cards use the
serif at display size, tabular figures where available.

## Colour usage

Navy (`--color-brand-primary`) for headings, rules and the primary chart
series. Gold (`--accent2-gold`) is the *only* secondary accent: a thin rule
under a section heading, a positive delta, a highlighted row. Never fill a
large area with gold. Background is white; cards are the warm off-white
`--color-bg-card`. Assume a grayscale printer: no meaning may rest on hue
alone — always pair a colour with a label, an arrow or a sign.

## Charts

Chart.js. Bars for comparisons, lines for trends over time, nothing else. Axis
labels always present, gridlines light, no 3-D, no doughnuts. Cap at five
series, palette in order. Every chart has a one-sentence caption under it
stating the takeaway, not the contents.

## Diagrams

Mermaid only when a dependency or an org relationship genuinely needs it —
`flowchart TD`, no more than eight nodes. A table is usually better.

## Components and when to use each

- `kpi-card` — the headline metric of a section, two to four in a row, at the
  top of the report or the top of a section. Never mid-paragraph.
- `section-lead` — the one-sentence conclusion that opens every section.
- `data-table` — comparison across periods or business units; right-align all
  numbers.
- `callout-quote` — a pulled statement from a stakeholder or a board question
  the report answers. At most one per report.

## Do / don't

- **Do** state the period explicitly in every chart caption and table header.
- **Do** mark estimates and forecasts as such, inline.
- **Don't** use emoji, exclamation marks, or an accent colour for emphasis in
  running text — use bold.
- **Don't** let a chart carry information that is not repeated in text.
- **Don't** add a company logo; the reader knows whose report this is.

components.name: kpi-card
components.description: One headline metric with a signed delta.
components.when_to_use: Two to four in a row at the top of the report or a section.
components.html:
Net revenue retention
114%
+6 pts vs. Q2

components.name: section-lead
components.description: The one-sentence conclusion opening a section.
components.when_to_use: Directly under every H2. Exactly one sentence.
components.html: Retention improved for the third consecutive quarter, driven entirely by the enterprise segment.

components.name: data-table
components.description: Period or unit comparison with right-aligned numbers.
components.when_to_use: Whenever more than three numbers are compared; prints cleanly.

components.name: callout-quote
components.description: A pulled stakeholder statement or board question.
components.when_to_use: At most once per report, to frame the section that answers it.
components.html:
Can we hold this margin through the migration?

Board, July meeting

charts.notes: Bars for comparison, lines for trend. Max five series, always a caption stating the takeaway.

diagrams.notes: flowchart TD, at most eight nodes; prefer a table.
